questions.q: Write the balanced half-reactions for the anode and cathode during rusting of iron in neutral aqueous medium, and give the overall reaction for formation of Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.
questions.a: Anode: Fe(s) → Fe²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻; Cathode: O₂(g) + 2H₂O(l) + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻(aq); Overall: 4Fe(s) + 3O₂(g) + 6H₂O(l) → 4Fe(OH)₃(s) → 2Fe₂O₃·3H₂O(s). A wrong answer (e.g., Fe → Fe³⁺ + 3e⁻ at anode, or H⁺ reduction at cathode) reveals confusion between acidic vs neutral mechanisms and ignorance that rust forms via Fe(OH)₃ dehydration, not direct Fe₂O₃ formation.

questions.q: Explain why rusting accelerates when iron is in contact with copper, but slows down when in contact with zinc, using the electrochemical series and galvanic cell concept.
questions.a: Cu²⁺/Cu (+0.34 V) is less negative than Fe²⁺/Fe (−0.44 V), so iron becomes anode and corrodes faster; Zn²⁺/Zn (−0.76 V) is more negative, so zinc becomes sacrificial anode protecting iron. A wrong answer (e.g., "copper protects iron because it's less reactive") reveals misunderstanding that the MORE reactive metal (lower reduction potential) oxidises preferentially in a galvanic couple.

questions.q: A 2.5 kg iron gate loses 12 g mass due to rusting over 6 months. Assuming uniform corrosion to Fe₂O₃, calculate the average corrosion current in mA. (F = 96500 C/mol, M_Fe = 56 g/mol)
questions.a: Mass loss = 12 g Fe → moles Fe = 12/56 = 0.214 mol. Each Fe loses 2e⁻ → moles e⁻ = 0.428 mol. Charge = 0.428 × 96500 = 41302 C. Time = 6 × 30 × 24 × 3600 = 1.555×10⁷ s. Current = 41302 / 1.555×10⁷ = 0.00266 A = 2.66 mA. A wrong answer using 3e⁻ per Fe (Fe→Fe³⁺) or forgetting time conversion reveals errors in oxidation state assignment or unit handling.

questions.q: Compare the initiation step of rancidity in linoleic acid (C18:2) vs oleic acid (C18:1). Why does linoleic acid oxidise faster? Use bond dissociation energies.
questions.a: Linoleic has −CH=CH−CH₂−CH=CH− (bis-allylic) with C−H BDE ≈ 335 kJ/mol; oleic has only allylic −CH=CH−CH₂− with BDE ≈ 360 kJ/mol. Lower BDE at bis-allylic position means easier H-abstraction by initiators (RO•, •OH), so linoleic acid oxidises ~40× faster. A wrong answer citing only "more double bonds" without bis-allylic distinction reveals superficial understanding of radical stability.

questions.q: A food manufacturer claims their chips "contain no added antioxidants" but use nitrogen flushing and opaque packaging. Evaluate whether this prevents rancidity completely. Justify with reaction mechanism.
questions.a: No — nitrogen flushing removes O₂ (slowing propagation) and opaque packaging blocks UV (slowing initiation), but trace O₂ permeates packaging and thermal initiation still occurs at storage temperature. Without chain-breaking antioxidants (e.g., BHT), propagation continues until termination by radical-radical coupling. A "yes" answer reveals ignorance that rancidity is a radical chain reaction requiring only ppm O₂ and thermal energy to sustain.

questions.q: Design a simple experiment to demonstrate that rusting is an electrochemical process requiring both anodic and cathodic sites. List materials, procedure, and expected observations with half-reactions.
questions.a: Materials: Two iron nails, agar-agar gel, K₃[Fe(CN)₆] (ferricyanide), phenolphthalein, NaCl. Procedure: Embed nails in gel with indicators; one nail straight, one bent sharply. Add NaCl droplets. Expected: Blue colour (Prussian blue, Fe³⁺ + [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻) at bent regions (anode, Fe→Fe²⁺); pink colour (phenolphthalein, OH⁻) at straight regions (cathode, O₂+2H₂O+4e⁻→4OH⁻). Half-reactions as in Q1. A poor answer omitting spatial separation of colours or half-reactions reveals failure to grasp electrochemical cell nature of corrosion.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Corrosion is an ______ redox process where a metal spontaneously oxidises in the presence of moisture and oxygen, forming metal oxides/hydroxides/carbonates; rusting of iron specifically involves Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻ (anode) and O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻ (cathode) forming hydrated Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.

Fill in the blank: Observe a rusted iron gate and a packet of stale chips at home — both show redox damage but differ fundamentally: the gate involves metal oxidation with oxygen reduction (______ cell), while chips involve radical chain oxidation of unsaturated fats.
What is Corrosion? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Corrosion is an electrochemical redox process where a metal spontaneously oxidises in the presence of moisture and oxygen, forming metal oxides/hydroxides/carbonates; rusting of iron specifically involves Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻ (anode) and O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻ (cathode) forming hydrated Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Corrosion?
questions.a: Students write the overall rusting reaction as 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃, ignoring water's role and the Fe(OH)₃ intermediate.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can write balanced half-reactions for iron rusting in acidic/neutral media, calculate equivalent weight of metal corroded using Faraday's laws, explain why rancidity accelerates at higher temperatures using Arrhenius concept, and design a prevention strategy (cathodic protection/antioxidant) for a given real-world scenario.
